html:
A war between the Roman Republic and Jugurtha, king of Numidia in North Africa, fought from about 112 to 106 BCE.

Jugurtha, a grandson of Masinissa, fought his cousins for the Numidian throne and killed both of them. When he took the city of Cirta, Italian traders there were massacred, and Rome declared war. For years Roman commanders did badly or made soft deals, and it was widely believed that Jugurtha had bribed senators. The historian Sallust, whose book is the main source, has him call Rome a city for sale.

The war made Gaius Marius famous. Elected consul in 107 BCE on anger at the nobles, he took command and opened the army to poor volunteers with no property, a change that would bind soldiers to their generals. His junior officer Sulla ended the war by persuading King Bocchus of Mauretania to hand Jugurtha over. Jugurtha was paraded in Rome and died in prison. The rivalry of Marius and Sulla later grew into civil war.
sum: A war between the Roman Republic and Jugurtha, king of Numidia in North Africa, fought from about 112 to 106 BCE.
